input: Scheduled routine: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products in production; merge when done.
task: Deepen (flagship 5, einvoice-preflight): score the NLCIUS, CIUS-RO, CIUS-PT and ZATCA folders of the phive-rules corpus on their CTestFiles.java good-case lists
errors: First corpus run had no official rules at all: plain-node.mjs needs `npm i --no-save slimdom fontoxpath`, and without it runPlain silently reports 'unavailable', so the PINT/ZATCA drops never fired and the numbers looked far worse than they were.
Seven corpus runs started in parallel; the CIUS-PT one hung at 4.4 GB, which is how the DT-CIUS-PT-111.1 regex blow-up was found.

CI validate failed: my flagships.yaml next: addition pushed einvoice-preflight's field to 2067 chars (cap 2000); shortened. portfolio/router/validate.py was not in run_workflow_locally's --for-changes output I read.

doc_friction.issue: Header did not say the official rules need slimdom+fontoxpath installed; without them the script silently scores built-in checks only. Worth a loud warning when plainAvailable() is false (not done here).
Top flagship (wall-framing-takeoff) is inputs_only and ai-bookkeeper's next item needs an LLM; no model endpoint or Hugging Face access from this container, so both were skipped for flagship 5.

deviations.why: Bare route drew research (weight 0.27); the scheduled prompt asks for revenue product work, so re-routed with --task, which picked ventures as prompt.md allows.

Rank 1 ai-bookkeeper's next item is the AI layer on one-off merchants, which needs a model; no Ollama, provider key or Hugging Face reachable here. Took flagship 5 (einvoice-preflight), the flagship with the clearest revenue path (EU mandates) and a buildable open item.

notes: Local verification: run_venture_tests einvoice-preflight ok (16.5s); pytest tests 368 passed incl. 3 new; run_workflow_locally --for-changes 11/16 workflows passed, the other 5 (agent-cross-review bots, portfolio-pages gate/deploy) are not runnable locally. Corpus: phive-rules 36d1f09, `--good`: PINT A-NZ 24/24, SG 15/16, ZATCA 8->18/19, NLCIUS 0/61 (54/61 with placeholder VAT/IBAN set aside), RO 0/10, PT hang -> 0/10 in ~3 s each (template placeholders). No post written about the agent doc: the README section is the agent-facing record.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: senior engineer: corpus harness, reading ~140 example files, four fixes with JS+Python tests

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
